requirements.requirement: The system must render a phase label (e.g., Phase I, II, III, IV) within the MessageBubble scorecard UI.
The system must display the consumer-friendly explanation text returned from S2 directly beneath or adjacent to the phase label.
The system must render the phase score contribution as a visible component within the scorecard.
The system must ensure the phase label, explanation, and score contribution are grouped as a single visual unit in the MessageBubble.
The system must render phase data only when valid interpreted output from S2 is present.
The system must maintain consistent styling with other scorecard measures rendered in MessageBubble.tsx.
The system must support markdown-compatible rendering for explanation text within MessageBubble.
The system must not break existing MessageBubble rendering for non-phase content.
The system must display a fallback label "Phase unavailable" when phase data is missing.
The system must hide the score contribution element when score data is missing or null.
The system must render phase information within 200ms of MessageBubble render time under normal conditions.
The system must ensure the phase label uses normalized formatting (e.g., "Phase II" not "2" or "II trial").
The system must ensure explanation text is human-readable and free of raw backend codes or abbreviations.
The system must ensure the explanation text length does not exceed UI constraints and is truncated or wrapped appropriately.
The system must render phase data consistently across multiple MessageBubble instances in a single chat session.
The system must ensure that the phase display contributes to the overall score visualization without duplication or double-counting.
The system must render explanation text that accurately reflects the mapped phase meaning produced by S2 without alteration.
The system must ensure that LLM-generated or mapped explanation text does not include hallucinated claims beyond the defined phase meaning.
The system must ensure that explanation text remains semantically consistent for identical phase inputs across sessions.
The system must ensure that explanation text avoids clinical jargon when a simpler alternative exists.
The system must ensure that explanation text communicates risk/uncertainty level appropriate to the phase.
The system must ensure that explanation text does not contradict the displayed phase label.
The system must ensure that explanation text is safe for consumer interpretation and does not imply guaranteed outcomes.
